In This Article Loading table of contents … Headquartered at Cairo International Airport, EgyptAir is the flag carrier of the African nation of Egypt and a member of  Star Alliance . The airline operates the majority of its routes between Egypt and Europe. However, EgyptAir does operate a few routes between Cairo and North America. And, if you plan on taking a long-haul flight between North America and Egypt, it may be worth it to book in business class. In general, EgyptAir business class isn’t considered to be one of the top business-products in the airline industry. And cash prices for long-haul EgyptAir flights can be rather high. So, if you still want to make your EgyptAir journey as comfortable as possible while keeping your out-of-pocket costs low, you should consider booking an EgyptAir business-class flight with points or miles. Since EgyptAir is a member of Star Alliance, there are a few partner frequent flyer programs through which you can book EgyptAir business-class award flights. Each of these programs, however, charges different rates for partner award flights. Likewise, some frequent flyer programs are easier to earn miles with than others because they accept transfers from major U.S. credit card rewards programs. So, in this article, we’ll take a look at some of the best programs through which to book Egypt Air business-class award flights. We’ll also take a brief look at what you can expect when flying in EgyptAir business class. What to Expect in EgyptAir Business Class The amenities and experience offered in EgyptAir business-class depend on the type of aircraft you’re flying on as well as the length of your flight. The following table includes basic information about the business-class cabin on each aircraft type in the EgyptAir fleet, including the number of business-class seats, seat configuration, seat pitch, seat width and entertainment screen size: Aircraft type Number of business-class seats Business-class seat configuration Seat pitch Seat width Entertainment screen size Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner 30 1-2-1 46 inches 22-27 inches 18 inches Boeing 777-300 49 2-3-2 76 inches 20 inches 15.4 inches Boeing 737-800 24 2-2 48 inches 19.8 inches 9 inches Boeing 737-800NG 16 2-2 60 inches 20.5 inches 9 inches Airbus A330-300 36 2-2-2 60 inches 20 inches 15.4 inches Airbus A321neo 16 2-2 48 inches 24 inches 13 inches Airbus A320neo 16 2-2 48 inches 24 inches 13 inches Airbus A350-900 30 1-2-1 44 inches 22 inches 19 inches Among the aircraft types listed above, the best business-class product is found on the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, which features lie-flat seats in a reverse herringbone configuration (offering maximum privacy), the largest personal entertainment screen in the fleet and an adjustable reading light. The next-best business-class products are found on Boeing 777-300 and Airbus A330-300 aircraft, which both offer lie-flat seats (although the seats on the Boeing 777 are “angle” lie-flat seats and not true lie-flat seats). Both of these aircraft also offer relatively large 15.4-inch entertainment screens. Plus, the newest addition is also a great option. The Airbus A350-900 began in February 2026 and includes 30 business class suites with direct aisle access. After that, you have all of the other aircraft in the EgyptAir fleet, which are used for medium- and short-haul flights. The business-class product on these aircraft is relatively unimpressive and is essentially the same as economy class with more legroom and improved dining and beverage options. For the purposes of this article, we’ll focus mostly on the experiences and amenities offered in business class on long-haul EgyptAir flights. As mentioned above, the business-class product on EgyptAir Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner aircraft features 18-inch personal entertainment screens and complimentary Wi-Fi. Unfortunately, there have been many users who have reported that these features were slow or entirely unavailable during their long-haul EgyptAir flight. Business-class passengers on long-haul EgyptAir flights can choose from one of several main course options, which might include dishes like grilled beef with creamy mushroom sauce, grilled chicken with rosemary demi-glace sauce, grilled shrimp with lemon butter sauce or vegetarian farfel pasta. You’ll also receive an appetizer, salad and a dessert and a selection of cheeses to follow your meal. EgyptAir is a dry airline, meaning that they don’t serve alcoholic beverages on board. However, business-class passengers will be able to choose from a selection of non-alcoholic beverages, including hot chocolate, cappuccinos, lattes, soft drinks, fresh juices and more. Business-class passengers on EgyptAir long-haul flights will also receive an amenity kit contained in a stylish branded bag. This amenity kit is actually fairly extensive compared to business-class amenity kits from other airlines and includes an eye shade, socks, lip balm, a shoehorn, a wooden hairbrush, hand sanitizer, a branded pen, a toothbrush, toothpaste and earplugs. All passengers on long-haul EgyptAir flights will also receive a pillow and blanket. According to most consumer reports, the pillow and blanket provided are fairly basic and not particularly comfortable. And, of course, your EgyptAir business-class experience will start before you even board your flight. Business-class passengers are entitled to priority treatment at the airport, including priority check-in, priority baggage handling, priority boarding and more. EgyptAir passengers ticketed in business class are also entitled to complimentary access to any of the EgyptAir business-class lounges in Cairo Airport (of which there are several). Plus, since EgyptAir is a member of Star Alliance, EgyptAir business-class passengers can also access Star Alliance partner airport lounges around the world. To see if there are any Star Alliance lounges at a specific airport, you can use the  Lounge Finder tool  in the My10x web app. Finally, EgyptAir business-class passengers on international flights are allowed to check up to two pieces of baggage (with a maximum weight of 32 kilograms each) and are allowed to bring up to two pieces of hand luggage (with a maximum weight of 8 kilograms each). EgyptAir business-class passengers on domestic flights are allowed to check one piece of baggage (with a maximum weight of 32 kilograms) and are allowed to bring up to two pieces of hand luggage (with a maximum weight of 8 kilograms each). Baggage rules may vary based on route, so be sure to check what your specific ticket/route offers. Best Programs Through Which You Can Book EgyptAir Business Class As previously mentioned, EgyptAir is a member of Star Alliance, which means there are a few different partner frequent flyer programs through which you can book EgyptAir business-class award flights. However, each frequent flyer program prices partner award flights differently, so the same EgyptAir award flight award might require more miles through one program than through another. Plus, certain frequent flyer programs are much easier to earn miles with because they allow transfers from major U.S. credit card rewards programs. So, with these factors in mind, let’s take a look at some of the best frequent flyer programs through which to book EgyptAir business-class award flights. Air Canada Aeroplan One of the best Star Alliance partner frequent flyer programs through which to book EgyptAir business-class award flights is the  Air Canada Aeroplan  program. Aeroplan generally prices Star Alliance partner awards according to its zone-and-distance award chart, subject to availability, fees and program rules, which means that it’s possible to find outsized value (exceeding 1 cent per point) on these redemptions. For example, we found a round-trip EgyptAir business-class award flight itinerary between New York (JFK) and Cairo (CAI) for 140,000 Aeroplan points and about 183 Canadian Dollars (about $133) in taxes and fees. If you were to book the exact same flights with cash through the EgyptAir website, it would cost you about $3,040. So, factoring in the taxes and fees you’d have to pay for the award flight, this redemption would give you a value of about 2.1 cents per point, which is solid. One of the biggest advantages of the Air Canada Aeroplan program is that it’s a 1:1 transfer partner of many of the major U.S. credit card rewards programs, including American Express Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One Rewards and Chase Ultimate Rewards. This makes it very easy to earn Aeroplan points if you have a credit card from one of the aforementioned issuers. Avianca LifeMiles Another great program through which to book EgyptAir business-class award flights is the  Avianca LifeMiles program . Just like Air Canada Aeroplan, this program uses a series of fixed award charts to price EgyptAir award flights, so you should be able to find EgyptAir awards that offer outsized value per mile through this program. For instance, we found a round-trip EgyptAir business-class award itinerary between New York (JFK) and Cairo (CAI) for 160,000 miles and about $104 in taxes and fees. If you were to book the same flights with cash through the EgyptAir website, it would cost you about $3,040. Thus, accounting for the taxes and fees paid for the award flight, this redemption would give you a value of about 1.8 cents per mile, which is decent. The Avianca LifeMiles program is also a 1:1 transfer partner of most of the major U.S. credit card rewards programs, including American Express Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One Rewards, Citi ThankYou Rewards and Wells Fargo Rewards. So, if you have a credit card from any of the aforementioned issuers, earning Avianca miles is relatively easy. The Bottom Line In general, the overall consensus among travel enthusiasts is that EgyptAir’s business-class product is rather lackluster and doesn’t justify the high cash prices charged for these tickets. While EgyptAir business class does include certain premium amenities (such as lie-flat seats, complimentary meals, amenity kits, airport lounge access and more), there are many aspects of this business-class product that fail to impress. Entertainment systems and Wi-Fi often don’t work on these flights, the meal service doesn’t include Egyptian cuisine, the food often isn’t very fresh, the bedding you’ll receive is very basic and EgyptAir doesn’t serve alcoholic beverages onboard. Nonetheless, if you’re planning a trip to Egypt on EgyptAir, flying in business class is still preferable to economy class. And the best way to get into EgyptAir business class while keeping your out-of-pocket costs low is to book with points and miles. In terms of booking Egypt Air business-class award flights, your two best options are typically the Air Canada Aeroplan program and Avianca LifeMiles program. Technically, you can also book these awards through the EgyptAir Plus frequent flyer program as well as the GOL Smiles program. However, these programs don’t allow transfers from credit card rewards programs and are also very difficult to use. Luckily, both Aeroplan and LifeMiles price EgyptAir award flights according to fixed award charts. This means that you should be able to find outsized value (exceeding 1 cent per mile) on these redemptions. 					Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card				 New to the world of points and miles? The
